overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the board could discuss the investigation in open session, and it was not required to give individuals discussed specific notice. Other allegations were declined as outside the OML.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board discussed her reputation, character, and mental health in open session when it should have gone into executive session under Purpose 1.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing the topic in open, rather than executive, session.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the board had to give her and others discussed at the May 31 meeting specific notice that they would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law does not require specific notice to an individual unless a public body plans to convene in executive session under Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a board member publicly slandered her, the town administrator, and other board members; this alleges violations of laws outside the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: This determination concerns only compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, thus we decline to review allegations of violation of any other laws.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a board member discussed personal matters in public and disclosed matters from an earlier executive session; the AG declined to review these.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not prevent public bodies from discussing personal matters in open meetings, nor require individuals present for executive session to keep matters discussed confidential.
